subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: Should plugin text transforms continue to apply to structured tool-call argument strings by default, or should OpenClaw add a path/tool-argument-safe boundary for filesystem and executable arguments?
rationale: Current main intentionally restores transformed structured arguments before tool execution, while this issue shows the same blind replacement primitive can silently misroute path-bearing file operations; changing it affects public plugin/provider semantics.

options.title: Add a safe executable-argument boundary
options.body: Keep prompt/display transforms but skip or narrowly gate replacements for path-like and executable tool arguments, with focused regression coverage and an upgrade note for plugin authors.

options.title: Keep current transform semantics
options.body: Preserve structured argument transforms as a plugin contract and document that plugins needing path safety must implement their own `before_tool_call` policy.

options.title: Move argument transforms to explicit hooks
options.body: Stop using `registerTextTransforms` for executable arguments and require plugins to opt into tool-specific decoding through `before_tool_call` or a new typed contract.

recommendation.title: Add a safe executable-argument boundary
recommendation.body: Keep prompt/display transforms but skip or narrowly gate replacements for path-like and executable tool arguments, with focused regression coverage and an upgrade note for plugin authors.

likelyOwner.reason: The text-transform surface originated in steipete's commit and this decision is about that public plugin/provider boundary.
